what.text: This page follows refugees from the Republic of the Congo living in France, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 6636 refugees from the Republic of the Congo in France, 50.5% of all refugees from the Republic of the Congo.
France is the largest host of refugees from the Republic of the Congo, followed by South Africa, the United States and Canada.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Congo in 1993, 1997 to 1999, 2002 and 2016, with the Ntsiloulous in the later years.
The fact pack does not give other reasons why people left.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1995 at 146 refugees.
The figure is at its highest at the end of 2025, and the main years of displacement in the data are 2012 to 2013 and 2018 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in France.
These are year-end totals for France only, reported to UNHCR.
